The text differential's control (the emitted float32 writer capped at six significant digits in memory, required red on the text comparison against the Go engine) rides here too: about 1 s on the author's machine. The accessor/descriptor agreement's two controls (a cook accessor pair swapped and a block pointer slot moved through go build -overlay, each required to red exactly its own fields) ride here too. The numbering walk's control (the grouped walk planted in the emitter through go test -overlay: arms_ptr and maps_pointers must red) and the float NaN control (table_widen_f32's bit surgery replaced by the hardware conversion through go test -overlay: the signalling NaNs must red) ride here too. The keyed accessor's control (the None half, the E.Max half and the shift taken out of table_enums.rs in turn, each required to red exactly its own clause) rides here too. The map writer's sort control (each writer's sort made a no-op, each required to red its own clause) rides here too. The cook of maps and lists' three controls (the carve laying a map's entries unsorted, an array unaligned, and a 128-bit holder's extent at the floor of eight, each through go build -overlay with the gate rebuilt against the regenerated mapdemo, listdemo and widelistdemo crates and required red on its own line) ride here too: about 60 s on intel, most of it the crate builds. Each rebuilds the compiler under an overlay and regenerates the corpus, about 12 s on the studio. The packet wide-text control removes the generated reader's surrogate pairing and requires the harness's bit-flip agreement with C++ to fail. Beside them, the all-port differential's planted-bad-pattern control changes one byte of a scratch answer tree and requires the comparison to go red and name wire/Scene; both halves of that control run on a t.TempDir(), with no toolchain, so the Squirrel lens still has a blade on a host carrying none of the other ports. It costs milliseconds. Beside them, the resource-bounds negative control (make/schema-squirrel-resource-bounds.mk) runs the planted-pattern gate over the port's allocation counter and depth cap: pure Go, no sq interpreter, so it is another pull-request blade for the Squirrel lens. The packet FINITE-FLOAT control (SPEC.md §4.3) drops the vendored serialize.nut's read test at both widths in memory (internal/codegen/squirrel/finite_test.go) and must red exactly the sixty-three non_finite_float read vectors of test/packet-finite/squirrel/main.nut while its write traps and bit-exact round trips stay green; one generate and one sq run, well under a second. The TABLE finite-float controls (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.3) remove one check at a time in memory (internal/codegen/squirreltable/nonfinite_test.go and nonfinite_forms_test.go): the variable read, the retained unknown entry's test and the variable writer, then the message read and writer and the fixed read and writer; each must red exactly that check's rows while the rest stay green; seven sq runs, about two seconds. The FLOAT-PARITY controls (internal/codegen/squirreltable/floatparity_test.go) put the old behaviour back in memory and must red exactly the rows the Go engine says it gets wrong: the variable read's compressed-float clamp removed (the rows the engine clamps), the message quantizer at one rounding in double (the fuzz rows where it parts from ir.TableMessageQuantize), an over-count message index clamped rather than refused (the over-count rows), and CookMeasure without its walk (the non-finite rows); four sq runs, under a second. Beside them, the hostile-corpus runner's planted reader (2.6 s on the studio) must go red; the nightly fuzzer's control patches the emitted load's array-frame bound and requires the wire differential to go red (1.8 s on the studio: it is the differential under a plant, not the nightly campaign, which schema-squirrel-nightly-fuzz.yml runs on its own schedule); and the generated-code lint gate's three plants (a refused statement, a trailing space, a blank-line run, each named by file and rule) run in under a second. The row installs the pinned interpreter (make/squirrel.mk's dist-squirrel) through its squirrel field, which must match test/conformance/squirrel/ci.json.
